gaps.note: MegaETH. The public stateless validator has now gone unrun for six cycles (L-626 inconclusive again in theme-closed-producers-2: fetched at e1618ed7, not built). It is the only public re-execution that compares the closed producer's full post-state, and evidence for that producer still covers Swap events, 3,741 v3 style swaps and receipts compared by status and logs. Liquidity removals, fee collections, burns and sync, settle or take inside reverted frames have never been compared with an independent post-state. The mega-reth v2.2.3 execution cache question (L-732) also stays unknown because the fork is not public.

Monad. theme-monad-emitter-blocks shows the PoolManager is compiled (estimate 285,084 bytes against a bound of 778,528) and that validators run Dual by default, so the compiled code is what validators execute. The harness that compared compiled with interpreted results stubbed runtime symbols and used a hand-patched evmc header in place of the category-labs/evmc commit of the release, and the asmjit commit was not pinned to the release submodule (the unit's own low lead). Mined Monad transactions have not been replayed through the native path of that harness from the parent-block storage cycle 13 collected. Because RPC nodes only check validators' headers on mined inputs, a compiled-only fault on an input nobody has mined yet is exactly what an ordinary account could be first to send.

Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain and Elysium had no unit in cycle 15. The ArbOS upgrade announced for Elysium about four weeks after 2026-11-09 (high leads L-001 and L-134) falls in the first week of December, before or at the next cycle. The nitro v3.13.0-rc.9 build the endpoints report is still private, and no reading of what the upgrade changes for the ElysiumCoreWriter predeploy and the HyperCore read precompile exists.

The seven ETH-gas OP Stack chains had no network unit in cycle 15, for the second cycle running. Lagoon (L-352 and L-525, both high) targets OP Sepolia and Unichain Sepolia on 10 December 2026 and OP Mainnet and Unichain on 11 January 2027, and nobody has read the predeploy implementations it installs at 0x4200..0022 to 0x28 and 0x30. The forks angle of cycle 15 was carried only by the Celo/X Layer, Polygon/BSC/Avalanche and Tempo/Arc units.

BNB Smart Chain. established-l1 observed that bsc-rpc.publicnode.com (reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix) returns an empty eth_getLogs result for block 135,483,276, which holds PoolManager logs on 48.club. Earlier BSC log censuses (currency lists behind F-093, the sSAC rebase history of F-091, mined-swap windows) were not checked for endpoint dependence; L-464 asked the same for bsc.api.pocket.network and is still open. Jenner on 2026-12-08 02:30 UTC still needs the full rerun, and the unpublished v1.8.2-4e1c8247 build remains untied to source.

Arc. All three public endpoints are now tested (stablecoin-l1), but the release each permissioned validator runs is unknown (L-688 inconclusive). Releases v0.8.0 to v0.8.4 carry the reth execution cache fault that Arc fixed later. Which validators, if any, still produce blocks on those releases has no source.

HyperEVM. The validator's revm and ruint versions are still unknown (L-618 inconclusive; the only lead is a DeepWiki summary of hyper-evm-sync naming revm 19.2.0, a secondary source). theme-closed-producers-2 ran about 25,000 of 84,543 multi-step v3 groups that may hold a 512 bit product. The archive client is the only re-execution and its header check against the validator's blocks is still unsourced (critic cycle 10).

Polygon. The established-l1 profile for 137 L2 repeats the statement that Salvador is the first BlockAlloc use on non-system accounts, which the verifier refuted on chain (WPOL 0x0d500B1d8E8eF31E21C99d1Db9A6444d3ADf1270 was deployed by an ordinary transaction and rewritten at block 62,278,656). Nobody compared the WPOL code before and after that rewrite for balanceOf and transfer behaviour toward a contract holder such as the PoolManager.

Tempo. The T15 zone path was read only for the debit side of a take. The refund and claim side of the zone portal (who sends the refund transaction, whether a parked refund for originator PoolManager can be released by any account, and whether zone withdrawals to Tempo can name the PoolManager and be submitted by any account) was not read, and that side decides whether an ordinary account can bracket the credit with sync and settle.

Celo. Mined-swap evidence is 428 swaps in one 540,000 block window, because forno caps eth_getLogs at 5,000 blocks. No removal or fee collection on Celo has been checked against the source, on either of the two backends behind forno.

leads.question: In the T15 zone portal source at Tempo v1.19.1 (the code that TIP-1094 gates), which function sends a failed-deposit refund to the originator, who may call it, and can any account release a parked refund whose originator is the PoolManager in a transaction it sends? Likewise, can any account submit the transaction that pays a zone withdrawal to a Tempo address, and can that address be the PoolManager?
leads.why: If any account can make the portal pay the PoolManager inside its own transaction, it can call sync(token), trigger the payment and settle, booking someone else's refund or withdrawal as its own payment (PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). That turns the low info item of stablecoin-l1 into an unprivileged theft path on Tempo from 15 December 2026.

leads.question: Can the MegaETH stateless validator fetched at e1618ed7 in theme-closed-producers-2.work be built with the Rust toolchain already on this machine (cargo --version, rustc --version) and the vendored dependencies, without installing anything? If yes, run it in block list mode over the blocks holding PoolManager removals, fee collections and the 87 take-in-reverted-frame transactions; if no, name the single missing artifact.
leads.why: The closed producer is the only executor of MegaETH blocks and no public re-execution has compared its post-state for liquidity removals. A producer-only arithmetic or state fault on such inputs is an unprivileged path to take or lock LP funds.

leads.question: Rebuild the theme-monad-emitter-blocks harness against the exact asmjit and category-labs/evmc commits pinned by the monad v0.16.7 submodules, with the real runtime symbols in place of stubs, then replay the cycle 13 mined PoolManager transactions and the nine per-path batteries through the native path. Does any call return different bytes, gas or storage from the interpreter?
leads.why: Validators run compiled code by default and RPC nodes only verify inputs that have been mined. A compiled-only fault on an unmined input could be triggered first by an ordinary account, and the current harness evidence rests on substitutes for two native dependencies.

leads.question: On the first day the announced ArbOS upgrade is live on Elysium (L-001, L-134), what code sits at the ElysiumCoreWriter predeploy and the HyperCore read precompile, and what do they answer to the PoolManager call shapes (empty calldata with value, balanceOf(PoolManager), transfer(to,amount), the IHooks selectors) through eth_call from the PoolManager address? Does the upgrade add a system path that moves native HYPE or a pooled token held by the PoolManager?
leads.why: A new system contract that accepts value or answers balanceOf with a value an ordinary account can change inside one transaction is a P1 or P3/P4 lever against the PoolManager's balance.

leads.question: Do the Base B20 token precompile and the BSC Jenner CAS20 tokens redirect a transfer by a pattern in the recipient address, or call out to another contract during a transfer, as Tempo's TIP-1094 zone deposit addresses do? Read the transfer path of each in the client source the endpoints run.
leads.why: Transfer of the Tempo T15 behaviour. A redirecting or calling transfer inside take changes where PoolManager funds go and opens the refund-bracketing question on those networks too.

leads.question: Have any CCTP or other permissionless-relay messages ever named a PoolManager of networks.json as mint recipient (MessageReceived or MintAndWithdraw events with mintRecipient equal to the PoolManager)? Which networks' native USDC can be minted to the PoolManager in a relay transaction an arbitrary account sends?
leads.why: Transfer of the Lagoon relay clearance on OP Mainnet and Unichain to every network with CCTP. A permissionless relay lets the relayer bracket the mint with sync and settle and book the funds of whoever bridged them.
